prompt.name: Framed Print Fine Art Portrait
prompt.content:
Transform the subject of this photograph into a bold graphic illustration with
heavy outlines, a limited flat colour palette and strong contrast.

Keep the subject clearly recognisable. Simplify detail rather than adding it —
avoid thin lines and fine gradients.

Surround the subject with a full-bleed background that fills the frame edge to
edge: large flat colour blocks, a thick circular halo behind the subject, and
simple repeating shapes filling the remaining space.

Leave no white or empty areas. Output flat 2D artwork only. Never draw a tote
bag, garment or any physical product. Do not return a photograph.

prompt.name: Red Carpet — Female
prompt.content:
Create a single, ultra-premium cinematic awards-night portrait in a 2:1 landscape format (aspect ratio exactly 2:1), designed as the photographic base plate for a luxury commemorative keepsake. This image must contain absolutely NO text, NO laurel wreath and NO name — those are added separately in production. The ONLY graphic element to render is the thin gold border described below. Otherwise deliver a clean photographic plate.

LIKENESS — ABSOLUTE PRIORITY: Reproduce the exact face, bone structure, skin tone, eye colour and hair of the person in the uploaded reference photograph with total fidelity. The finished subject must be unmistakably the same individual. Preserve their natural skin tone precisely with rich, true-to-life warmth — no lightening, no smoothing away of natural texture, no alteration of ethnicity or features.

SUBJECT & POSITION: A radiant, confident woman in her moment of triumph on awards night. Position her on the RIGHT side of the frame — head and shoulders occupying roughly the right 40% of the image, turned slightly toward camera, looking at the viewer with a warm, genuine, beaming smile. HEADROOM: leave a clear gap of about 5% of the image height between the top of her head/hair and the top edge of the image — her head must NOT touch or crowd the top edge. Her body extends downward and may run off the BOTTOM edge of the frame. She holds an elegant abstract gold trophy at chest height — a smooth, sculptural, wholly original flame-like design (NOT any real or trademarked award statuette). Poised, star-quality presence; she is clearly the centre of attention.

HAIR & MAKEUP — fresh-from-the-salon (do NOT change the hairstyle): Keep her exact hairstyle, cut, length, natural colour, parting and texture from the reference. Render it as the best possible version of that same style — freshly salon-styled and blow-dried, clean, glossy and healthy, smoothed with flyaways tamed, natural volume and shape at their most flattering, catching soft light. Flawless professional red-carpet makeup that enhances rather than changes her features: an even, radiant complexion with natural skin texture retained, subtly defined eyes, groomed brows and a refined lip — polished, never heavy or mask-like.

WARDROBE: A sophisticated black evening gown with a V-neckline, couture quality, subtle sheen. Refined diamond drop earrings and a delicate diamond necklace. Understated glamour.

SETTING & CROWD: A prestige awards auditorium behind her, bathed in warm golden light with a soft glow spilling down from above at the top centre of the frame. An audience of elegantly dressed guests fills the background on the LEFT and CENTRE, softly out of focus. These guests face FORWARD — turned toward the camera and the subject, applauding and celebrating her, all attention flowing toward her. No one facing away or turned to the back of the hall. The crowd on the left sits deeper in shadow — present and visible but dim and moody, softly lit so it reads as atmospheric depth rather than bright detail. A few out-of-focus camera flashes and bokeh highlights glint on the right side behind her. Cinematic shallow depth of field: the crowd soft, the subject razor sharp.

PALETTE & LIGHTING: Deep warm blacks and browns, rich champagne-gold ambient light, warm cinematic key light on her face, gentle rim light separating her hair from the darker background. The left side falls into warm shadow; the light concentrates around and above the subject. Celebratory, aspirational, luxurious. Editorial-grade retouching with natural skin texture retained.

GOLD BORDER (the only graphic element — follow EXACTLY): Draw a single thin champagne-gold (#E5C87E) rectangular border line, a fine continuous unbroken hairline, framing the whole image. Its inset from the edges MUST be uneven and this is critical: the gap above and below the line (top and bottom) must be TWICE as large as the gap left and right. Concretely: inset the line about 5% of the image width from the LEFT and RIGHT edges, and about 10% of the image height from the TOP and BOTTOM edges. The top and bottom gaps must be visibly, obviously larger than the side gaps — NOT equal on all four sides. The subject stands in front of and overlaps this line while the line sits in front of the blurred background crowd, creating a layered depth effect. No other lines, boxes, text or shapes anywhere.

TECHNICAL: Ultra-high resolution, razor-sharp focus on the face, photorealistic, print quality. 2:1 landscape aspect ratio. Subject on the right, atmospheric shadowed crowd on the left and centre. Single-pass final image.

DO NOT: no text of any kind; no laurel or wreath; no name; no year, date or number; no second or double border, no ornate/patterned frame; no real or brand-named statuettes (no Oscar / BAFTA / Emmy / Globe shapes); no real award-show or brand logos; no watermarks; no change to hairstyle, likeness or skin tone; no extra limbs or hands.

prompt.name: Partners in Crime
prompt.content:
Partners in Crime
v2.12

ROLE
You are generating a single flat "getaway" illustration for a personalized gift product. Input: one reference photo showing either (a) two people together, or (b) one person and one pet together. Output: one 21:9 (2:1) landscape illustration, photoreal semi-realistic digital-painting style and brand-safe — fun and heroic, never menacing, violent, or gory.
STEP 0 — READ THE REFERENCE PHOTO
Look at the attached reference photo and determine the configuration:
TWO PEOPLE: extract both people. The driver takes the wheel; the other is the passenger holding the diamond.
PERSON + PET: the person always drives. The pet is always the passenger — never behind the wheel, never touching the wheel, paws resting in its own lap or against the door.
Preserve each subject's exact likeness — facial features, hairstyle, glasses, skin tone, and, for a pet, its specific coloring, markings, and coat texture — matching the reference photo precisely and photographically, rendered with the soft, cinematic, semi-realistic quality described in STYLE below. Clothing should match what subjects are wearing in the reference photo, adapted only enough to suggest a light breeze (see SPEED & MOTION). Clothing color is a hard match, not an approximation — if the reference shows a red sweater, render true red, never a lighter/pastel shade like pink. Any clothing shown on a subject in the reference photo must always be visible in every generation — never omitted. A pet never wears glasses, hats, or any other accessory unless that exact item is visible on it in the reference photo — do not borrow the driver's glasses or anything else it is wearing. The only items ever added to a pet are the collar, tag, and pearls described under THE LOOT.
CAMERA, DIRECTION & COMPOSITION
This is a TIGHT, low, cabin-focused shot, not a wide hero shot of the whole car.
CAMERA ANGLE: a three-quarter tracking angle — the camera rides alongside the convertible, slightly behind and outboard of it, looking diagonally across the windscreen so both faces are seen through the glass. This is not a side-on, profile, or broadside shot of the car's flank.
The convertible's cabin — windscreen, both faces, doors — fills roughly the right 45–50% of the frame, large and close, cropped tightly enough that the car extends past the right edge of the canvas. Do not let the cabin balloon past roughly half the frame — if its left edge is landing earlier than 45% from the left, it is too zoomed in. The exterior wing mirror is door-mounted, positioned just behind the base of the windscreen pillar rather than out on the front fender, and is part of the cabin — it must never extend further left than the horizontal center line of the frame.
The hood, grille, and headlights are NOT a visible focal point. At most a small hint of front fender may show low in frame — do not render a prominent grille or lit headlights front-and-center. CRITICAL: this hood/fender hint must also stay right of the horizontal center line, same as the mirror — check the bottom of the frame separately from the middle of the frame, since a shot can pass the mirror check and still fail if the hood or a wheel pokes left of center lower down. The whole vehicle, top to bottom, stays right of center.
The pursuing police car sits smaller and more distant, positioned horizontally at roughly 44–50% of the canvas width from the left edge. HARD FLOOR: never further left than 40% of canvas width, including the light bar on its roof — in production this zone sits behind a fixed logo graphic that is wider than the bare empty margin described below, so anything left of 40% risks being covered by it entirely. If the gap to the convertible looks tight, move the police car right or leave more dust between the two cars — do not fix it by zooming the cabin in further. Its dust cloud, the convertible's own dust cloud, and a few flying banknotes all drift in the gap between the two cars — ALL of this must stay confined to that gap and never spread into the reserved left text zone. Banknotes stay LOW — at or below door height — never rising to windscreen height.
The leftmost ~25–30% of the frame MUST show open road, sky, and low desert scrub — the paved road, with its edge or a lane line visible, is a required part of this zone, not an optional one; do not leave it as bare, featureless ground with no road surface at all. Separately, this same zone must stay clear of anything else — no cacti, trees, poles, road signs, traffic signs, rock formations, cars, dust, or banknotes of any kind. Treat this as a hard minimum, not a target: the true safe distance is the police car's own 40% floor above, since the actual text/logo artwork used in production is wider than this bare minimum margin.
FIXED LAYOUT, NEVER MIRRORED: the police car and its dust must always be to the LEFT of the convertible's cabin. If it ends up right of the convertible, flip the image horizontally before returning it.
SPEED & MOTION — the defining feature of this scene, not a background detail
The entire desert and mountain backdrop is visibly streaked with long horizontal motion-blur — sharpest close to the car, progressively blurrier toward the horizon.
A large, ragged plume of dust billows up from the convertible's own rear tires, separate from and in addition to the police car's dust further behind.
Ears (if a pet), hair, and any loose clothing/fabric show only a subtle, natural amount of wind movement — never a dramatic streaming/flapping banner. This is especially true for the driver: do not invent long flowing hair motion on a subject with short, thinning, or receding hair — hair and any beard/facial hair move only slightly, staying close to the head and jawline.
Clothing stays physically attached to the body at all times — wind shows up only as small ripples or a light flutter at an existing edge, never as a separate flap or piece of fabric floating disconnected from the body.
Light is warm, low, and golden-hour: a warm amber-to-orange band sits low near the horizon, blending up into soft pale blue higher in the sky, with the sun low enough to cast long warm-toned shadows. A bright, neutral, overhead midday blue sky is a failure state — if the sky reads cool or flat, redo it warmer and lower.
EXCEPTION: the windscreen glass, both faces, and the money bag/pearls/diamond stay crisp and unblurred. This is a motion-panning photograph — the camera tracks alongside the convertible at the exact same speed, so the driver and pet render pin-sharp and fully in focus. Only the background, dust, and loose hair/fur/fabric carry motion blur. Zero blur may touch any skin, hair, or facial feature.
SUBJECTS & POSE
Exactly two subjects appear in the scene — the driver and the passenger described in STEP 0 — and nothing else. No extra people, no disembodied limbs, no third figure of any kind.
Both the driver and the passenger turn for a relaxed glance toward the camera riding alongside them. Expression is warm and genuinely happy — eyes with real warmth, corners of the mouth clearly upturned in a visible smile — never flat, neutral, closed-lip, or restrained, but also never an exaggerated wide-open grin. Both sit upright behind the windscreen with heads and shoulders clearly above the frame line. Hair and fur move per SPEED & MOTION above — even a single stray wisp lifting off the scalp on a balding subject counts as a violation. The driver's hand rests loosely on the wheel, simply rendered.
Pet posture (when applicable): the pet sits normally on the seat, chest toward the door. Front paws rest low against the top of the door panel itself, below the window opening, or on the seat cushion — never hooked, draped, or propped over the top rail of the door, and never raised to window/windscreen height or appearing to overlap the windscreen glass.
PET SCALE (when applicable)
The pet is rendered at a size natural to its real proportions relative to the person in the same reference photo — never human scale, never toy-like.
THE LOOT
A small cloth money bag, tied at the top with a "$" mark, rests ON THE SEAT in the gap between the seats — sitting at seat height, its top no higher than the seatback or the seated subjects' shoulders. Visible but modest, lower than either face, never covering it.
Person passenger (when there is one): holds a single large diamond raised in one hand out to the side — one clear, readable shape, no bigger than a head.
Pet passenger (when there is one) — collar and pearls:
COLLAR & TAG — CRITICAL: a bone-shaped or paw-shaped tag is the generic default for a dog collar — actively resist that default here. The tag must be heart-shaped, exactly matching the reference photo, in every single generation. If you notice yourself drawing a bone or paw shape, stop and redraw it as a heart instead. Same collar color as the reference too. This sits normally around the neck, and stays correct independently of anything happening with the pearls.
PEARLS — CRITICAL: the pet holds pearls at ONE single point in its mouth. From that one point, the entire strand hangs straight down as ONE line — a single clean strand dropping from the mouth to about chest height, nothing more. It must NEVER split into two visible strands, never loop or wrap around the neck, and never swing out to the side away from the body — it hangs straight down the front, close to the chest, like a single string dropped from the mouth. Round, connected beads, one continuous unbroken line. If you're unsure, draw it exactly like a single strand of a necklace that's been picked up by one end and left dangling — not worn.
No other accessories: the pet wears only what's described above (and its collar/clothing from the reference photo, per STEP 0) — never glasses, hats, bandanas, or anything else, even if the human subject is wearing them.
A few banknotes flutter loose in the car's wake, trailing off the boot, behind the car — never ahead of it.
VEHICLE, POLICE CAR & SCENE
A classic vintage 1950s/60s convertible, top down, chrome trim, tail fins, vivid teal paint. This is a hard rule — check the rendered color before returning the image; gold, tan, red, or any other color is a failure.
The windscreen glass is present, clean, and only lightly reflective in its chrome frame. Keep the chrome at the mirror/windscreen junction simple and single, not doubled or ornate.
The pursuing police car is the same design in every generation: a black-and-white two-tone 1950s sedan silhouette — rounded fenders, chrome bumper and grille, dark paint above the beltline and white paint below it, a single red-and-blue dome light centered on the roof. Lights flashing, comic and non-threatening, always behind and losing ground, matching the convertible's era.
STYLE — PHOTOREAL SEMI-REALISTIC DIGITAL PAINTING, NOT FLAT CARTOON
Render as a photoreal 3D / digital-painting illustration: soft cinematic lighting, realistic material textures, smooth gradient shading — like a high-end animated-movie poster aimed at adults, not a flat vector cartoon or comic panel.
NO bold black outlines around shapes. Edges are defined by lighting, shading, and soft rim-light, not ink linework.
Faces, fur, and fabric have real dimensional shading with smooth gradient transitions — not flat color blocks, not cel shading.
Likeness stays photographically accurate: real proportions, real skin/fur texture — refined, believable, a little glossy/cinematic. NOT childlike, not exaggerated like a kids'-cartoon mascot.
The dust cloud is a soft, realistic, photographic-feeling plume — not a graphic outlined "poof" shape.
Colors are warm and cinematic, with real depth and highlight detail — not flat/matte poster colors.
Self-test: if the image would look at home as a flat sticker or comic panel, it's too cartoonish — add back soft shading and cinematic lighting, remove any hard ink outline.
TEXT
No text, words, letters, or typography render anywhere in the image — the only exception is the "$" mark on the money bag. This includes badges, scripts, or model-name trim anywhere on the vehicle bodywork (for example a tail fin nameplate) — treat any such marking as a text violation. Do not leave a placeholder banner or shape beyond the empty left margin.
FORMAT
Single flat artwork, 21:9 (2:1) landscape aspect ratio. No borders, no collage panels, no extra frames.
FINAL SELF-CHECK — verify all of the following before returning the image:
Exactly two subjects in the whole frame — no extra people, no disembodied limbs.
Camera reads as a three-quarter tracking angle, never side-on/profile — the car's full flank is never visible in one straight line.
Both driver and passenger glance toward camera with a warm, genuine, visible smile.
Hair stays visually flat against the head.
Clothing color matches the reference exactly, and any clothing shown in the reference is present. Pet has no glasses, hat, or other accessory not shown in its own reference photo.
Real horizontal motion blur in the background; dust cloud from the convertible's own tires. Sky reads warm and golden-hour, not neutral midday blue.
Panning shot: faces and windscreen glass are pin-sharp; zero blur on skin/hair/face.
Cabin fills roughly the right 45–50% of the frame — not more. Door-mounted mirror and hood both stay right of the horizontal center line.
Police car sits at 44–50% of canvas width — never below the 40% hard floor, including its light bar. This floor exists to clear the actual logo artwork used in production, not just the bare empty margin.
If the gap to the convertible looks tight, the fix was moving the police car, not shrinking the cabin — check the cabin hasn't ballooned past 50% fill.
The reserved left zone shows an actual road — with a visible edge or lane line — not bare, featureless ground.
Money bag rests on the seat at seat height.
Collar and tag match the reference exactly, including tag shape — heart, never a bone/paw/disc default.
Pearls: ONE single strand only, hanging straight down from one bite point — no splitting into two strands, no looping around the neck, no swinging to the side. Round, fully connected, no gaps.
Pet's paws (if applicable) rest low on the seat/door panel, below window height — never hooked over the top rail or reaching windscreen height.
Convertible is teal.
No badge, script, or trim text anywhere on the bodywork, including the tail fin.
Diamond (if a person passenger) is a single clear held shape.
Pet (if present) is scaled naturally against the person.
Police car matches the convertible's 1950s/60s era.
No text or lettering anywhere except the "$" on the money bag.
Reads as photoreal, semi-realistic digital-painting — no bold ink outlines, no flat cartoon shading.

prompt.name: skysun
prompt.content: Create a single, ultra-premium cinematic superhero portrait in a wide 21:9 landscape, designed as a luxury commemorative keepsake. Photorealistic, feature-film quality. This image is a BACKGROUND PLATE — all typography is added afterwards in production. The numbered Fixed geometry below is a strict spec: hold those values identically across every generation. They are anchored to the FRAME, not artistic choices that may vary render to render. FIXED GEOMETRY — frame-anchored, identical every render 1. Format: wide 21:9 landscape. 2. Hero: right of centre, large and close to camera, shown from head to mid-calf — not a small distant figure. 3. Sky signal: exactly ONE. The projected light mark is roughly one-third (33%) of the image height across; its centre sits about 20% in from the LEFT edge and about 24% down from the TOP edge; it stays fully inside the upper-left quadrant and never touches any frame edge. A single beam originates low, immediately behind the hero, and travels diagonally UP and to the LEFT to the projected mark. 4. Left wall: a solid dark parapet whose flat top edge is fixed at 33–38% of the image height, held constant from the LEFT frame edge across to where the cape begins, then stepping gently DOWN toward the hidden corner. 5. Right ledge: rises at a SHALLOW, gentle angle from the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner, staying within the lowest ~15–20% of the frame at the right edge. 6. Cape reach: the cape's lower-left trailing edge reaches at least 15% of the frame WIDTH in from the left edge — anchored to frame position, not to the body's pose. 7. City height: the lit skyline rises to roughly HALF (≈50%) of the frame height, across the full width. 8. Text-backdrop zone: the lower-left rectangle running from the BOTTOM frame edge up to the wall's top edge (33–38%), and from the LEFT frame edge across to where the cape begins. Descriptive brief LIKENESS — ABSOLUTE PRIORITY: Reproduce the exact face, bone structure, skin tone, eye colour, hairline and hair of the person in the uploaded reference photograph with total fidelity. This is non-negotiable: the finished subject must be unmistakably the same individual. Preserve their natural skin tone precisely and render it with rich, true-to-life warmth and even, flattering light — no lightening, no smoothing away of natural texture, no idealising or slimming of the face, no de-ageing, no alteration of ethnicity or features. If the reference subject wears glasses, keep them. The face must never be obscured by mask, helmet, hood, shadow or cape. SUBJECT & POSE: A powerful, composed male hero standing at the corner of a high rooftop at night (framing and placement per Fixed geometry 2). Body turned three-quarters toward camera, chin level, gaze direct and calm — quiet authority rather than aggression. Feet planted, arms relaxed at his sides, shoulders squared. CAPE — LARGE, LONG AND DRAMATIC: A very long, voluminous cape caught in strong wind, billowing out to the LEFT and sweeping DOWN in a wide sculptural curve that fills much of the centre-left of the frame and trails low toward the lower third — long enough that its lower folds fall across and HIDE the rooftop corner behind it (reach per Fixed geometry 6). It is a major compositional element: expansive, flowing, with rich fabric. Charcoal outer surface with a warm bronze-amber lining catching the light. Never render it small, short, tight or close to the body. COSTUME — WHOLLY ORIGINAL DESIGN: A sculpted deep midnight-navy armoured suit with subtle matte textured panelling and fine seam detailing, fitted and modern. Burnished bronze edging at the collar, shoulders and forearm bracers. On the chest, a single ORIGINAL sculpted emblem: an abstract upward-pointing chevron enclosed in a smooth circular bezel, rendered in bevelled burnished bronze with a bright specular highlight along its edge — raised and metallic, not a flat printed graphic. The costume must be entirely invented and must not resemble any existing comic, film or television superhero. SETTING — FULL-WIDTH LIT CITY: A vast, richly detailed modern city skyline at night filling the FULL WIDTH of the frame on BOTH sides — tall, densely built towers, generic invented architecture, no recognisable real-world landmarks (height per Fixed geometry 7). The city is the key backdrop and must be prominent and clearly defined: thousands of pin-sharp warm and cool window lights, red rooftop beacons, and bright red-and-white traffic light-trails in the streets below on the right. Outside the text-backdrop zone the city is pin-sharp with only mild far-distance atmosphere — never compressed, pushed into the corners or off the edges, and never rendered as heavy bokeh or abstract blobs of light. The city sits BEHIND the foreground parapet and rises clearly ABOVE it; the wall and ledge never hide, replace or shrink it. (Inside the text-backdrop zone the city is deliberately darkened and defocused — see Text backdrop.) FOREGROUND — ROOFTOP CORNER: The hero stands at the corner of the rooftop, and the corner is HIDDEN BEHIND THE CAPE — centre-left, behind the sweeping fabric, not merely behind his body. To his left, the solid dark parapet WALL forms the dark backdrop for the name (top edge per Fixed geometry 4). To his right, a LOW ledge (per Fixed geometry 5) — not a steep or high diagonal, and the hero must not look raised on a platform. Keep the wall and ledge simple, dark and unlit. TEXT BACKDROP — DARKENED, DEFOCUSED ZONE (EQUAL STRENGTH TOP TO BOTTOM): Production overlays the customer's name across the text-backdrop zone (bounds per Fixed geometry 8). Across that ENTIRE zone — with EQUAL strength from the bottom edge all the way up to the wall's top line, not fading or weakening toward the top — apply two effects together: (1) UNDEREXPOSURE — render it 2.5–3 stops darker than the rest of the frame, a deep, near-black, even shadow with only faint texture and NO city lights, window glow or light-trails showing through anywhere; (2) DEFOCUS — render any city detail that would fall within the zone with heavy depth-of-field falloff, a soft diffused glow at most, never a sharp window or trail. The upper part of the zone, near the wall's top line, is the area most likely to leak lit windows in testing — treat it with EXACTLY the same darkening and defocus as the bottom; there must be no gradient where the bottom reads dark but the top still shows city. This treatment applies ONLY inside this zone; everywhere else the city stays pin-sharp and normally exposed. ATMOSPHERE — DRAMATIC STORM SKY: A turbulent, dramatic night storm. Heavy, roiling banks of dark cloud fill the sky, backlit with deep amber-bronze breaks. Forked lightning crackles across the UPPER-CENTRE and UPPER-RIGHT in warm amber-white bolts, illuminating the cloud edges — powerful and cinematic. Keep the UPPER-LEFT relatively free of lightning so the projected sky signal stays the dominant, cleanest light source there. Light rain falls across the whole frame as fine glinting streaks. Deep midnight-blue and near-black tonality overall. Keep the storm confined to the UPPER sky so it does not darken or crowd out the full-width lit city in the mid-band below. SKY SIGNAL — SINGLE, ANCHORED: One volumetric searchlight beam (origin, path, size and position per Fixed geometry 3) throws the hero's emblem onto the underside of the storm clouds in the upper-left — a BAT-SIGNAL-STYLE projection made of LIGHT, not a solid object. The chevron-in-circle shape is formed where the beam illuminates the cloud: a soft, luminous, glowing warm amber-bronze mark with feathered, slightly diffuse edges, storm-cloud texture visible within and through the glow so it reads as light cast on cloud, fully integrated into the sky. It must NOT look like a solid metallic ring, a 3D badge, a medallion, a coin or a rendered logo stamped, pasted or floating in front of the sky — no hard opaque sharp edges, no metallic shading — and equally NOT a flat, featureless white plate; it is glowing, feathered light with cloud texture inside it. The shape must still clearly and exactly match the chest emblem — an upward-pointing chevron inside a circular ring — just rendered in soft projected light rather than solid material. It reads as ONE clear corridor of light rising from behind the hero to the projected mark, with soft atmospheric scatter — not a spray of scattered shafts, and not multiple beams. PALETTE: Disciplined and restrained — deep midnight navy, near-black, and burnished bronze / warm amber as the single accent. Cool blue city lights only in the background. The storm lightning is warm amber-white and is on-palette. No competing colours, no red beyond distant tail-lights, no primary-colour comic palette. LIGHTING & MOOD: Cool blue rim light from behind separating him from the night sky, warm amber key light across his face and chest, deep contrast, with amber lightning flashes as dramatic accents in the upper sky. Heroic, aspirational, cinematic, still. Editorial-grade retouching with natural skin texture and pores retained. NO TEXT — ABSOLUTE REQUIREMENT: This image must contain NO text of any kind. No names, words, letters, numerals, captions, titles, logos, signage, building signs, billboards, watermarks or signatures, and no symbols resembling letters. The chevron-in-circle emblem is the ONLY graphic mark permitted, and it must not resemble any letter of any alphabet. COMPOSITION & TECHNICAL: Wide 21:9 landscape, all placements per Fixed geometry. Keep the face, chest emblem and sky signal well inside a central safe zone with generous margin at the extreme left and right edges. Ultra-high resolution, razor-sharp focus on the face, print quality. Single-pass final image. DO NOT: no text, letters, numbers or writing anywhere; a visible city light, window or light-trail ANYWHERE inside the text-backdrop zone (including the upper band near the wall line) is a FAILED render; any darkening or defocus OUTSIDE that zone; more than one sky signal, or a signal that drifts from the upper-left or changes size; a sky signal that looks like a solid metallic ring, 3D badge, medallion, coin or rendered logo stamped, pasted or floating on the sky (hard opaque sharp edges, metallic shading), OR a flat featureless white plate — it must instead read as soft glowing projected light on the storm cloud, feathered and with cloud texture visible within it; scattered, sprayed or multiple beams instead of one clean shaft; any emblem shape other than the chevron-in-circle in either the chest or the sky (no checkmark, V or M substituted); the city hidden, shrunk, compressed or pushed to the corners/edges by the wall, ledge, storm or sky; a small, short, tight or close-cropped cape; existing or trademarked superhero costumes, emblems, logos or characters; S-shields, bat motifs, spider motifs, star-and-stripe shields or plain lightning-bolt emblems on the costume; masks, helmets or hoods; real-world landmarks or brand signage; weapons; flying or mid-air pose; distortion of the subject's likeness or skin tone; extra limbs, hands or fingers.

prompt.name: new prompt
prompt.content:
Produce a single luxury monochrome portrait: a real black-and-white editorial photograph of the
subject, composited onto a solid pure-white knockout background — the way a high-end fashion
catalog (Net-a-Porter, SSENSE, Matches) shoots a studio portrait and drops it onto a flat colour
canvas in post, rather than photographing the background itself. The 3:4 portrait format fills the
whole wrap edge to edge. The subject is centred and carried large; the backdrop runs
seamlessly across the full width so the wrap has no visible join. Render into the image the
magazine title ICON (in red) and the city line above it (in black) — nothing else appears
anywhere in the frame. Both title and city line are treated the same way as the background:
printed graphic layers, not photographed elements.
LIKENESS — ABSOLUTE PRIORITY
Reproduce the exact face, bone structure, skin tone, and eye shape/colour of the person in the
uploaded reference photograph with total fidelity. The finished subject must be unmistakably the
same individual — no slimming, no de-ageing, no alteration of features or ethnicity.
FORMAT & FINISH
An ultra-wide 3:4 portrait editorial photograph, full-bleed and immersive, filling the frame edge to
edge. The subject herself — her skin, hair, suit, and the chair — carries the full quality of a real
medium-format monochrome photograph: fine natural grain, a soft rich tonal range, genuine
photographic depth and dimension.
The background is not a lit or photographed surface at all — it is a flat compositing canvas,
exactly like a knocked-out product-catalog background: imagine the subject shot separately in
the studio and then dropped onto a solid colour fill in post-production, the way fashion e-
commerce sites present studio portraits. This canvas is one single, perfectly uniform pure white
(RGB 255,255,255), with zero photographic properties of its own — no light source, no shadow,
no falloff, no grain, no gradient. Every pixel of it, from dead centre to the furthest corner, is the
exact same flat white value. There is no tile, panel, seam, or patch of a different shade
anywhere in it.
Every element on the subject is rendered strictly in black, white, and grey — skin tones, hair, the
navy suit, the chair — with zero colour saturation and no colour cast of any kind. The single
exception, described in full below, is the masthead title, which is the only source of colour
anywhere in the image.
HAIR — fresh-from-the-salon (do NOT change the hairstyle)
Keep her exact hairstyle, cut, length, natural colour, parting and texture from the uploaded
reference photograph — do not default to a generic style. Render it as the best possible version
of that same style: freshly salon-styled and blow-dried, clean, glossy and healthy, flyaways
tamed, natural volume and shape at their most flattering.
GLASSES — CONDITIONAL, MATCH THE REFERENCE
If the person in the uploaded reference photograph is wearing glasses, include glasses of a
similar style on her in the final image. If the reference photograph shows no glasses, do NOT
add glasses.
SUBJECT & FRAMING
(Unchanged — client confirmed this pose is good.)

The subject — a woman — sits at the centre of the frame, carried large, a three-quarter crop
from roughly the thigh up, in an ornate carved French fauteuil upholstered in dark damask. Both
the chair and her body are turned to a slight three-quarter angle — roughly fifteen to twenty-five
degrees off square — so one arm of the chair and one shoulder read nearer the camera than
the other, giving the pose depth and impact rather than a flat, head-on view. She sits with quiet
poise: legs crossed with the top knee angled across the body, one elbow resting on that raised
knee and the hand lifted to rest lightly against her chin or jaw, the other hand relaxed on the
thigh. Her head and gaze turn back to the camera, direct and quietly commanding, even as the
body stays angled. She wears an impeccably tailored midnight-navy trouser suit with a deep
lapel and a sculptural fabric brooch in a complementary dark tone, fine drop earrings, and her
hair and glasses styled per the HAIR and GLASSES sections above. The deep navy suit reads
as a rich, dark tone with strong, clean tonal separation against the pure white backdrop —
natural, confident contrast, no risk of merging. The dark upholstered chair adds further depth
and structure behind her. Soft directional key light from the front-left with gentle shadow and a
hint of rim brings dimension to the fabric without softening the overall contrast. Elegant,
flattering and refined.
MASTHEAD — A PRINTED GRAPHIC LAYER, THE ONE COLOUR ACCENT
Centred across the top of the frame, treat the magazine title as a printed graphic element
applied to the cover — like real masthead type on the flat white canvas described above, not
something lit or photographed within the scene. It reads exactly ICON: one continuous unbroken
word, four large high-contrast Didone serif capitals (I, C, O, N) touching in a normal, even line —
never split by a hyphen, dash, gap, or line break. Render it in a rich, deep, saturated publication
red: a classic solid magazine-masthead red, matte and flat, distinctly warm rather than orange
or pink. This red is the only coloured element anywhere in the image, fully contained within the
letterforms, with no bleed, glow, or tint reaching the skin, hair, suit, chair, or backdrop. The
letterforms have clean, hard edges — no soft antialiased colour halo or warm tint bleeding into
the white background immediately around them. The subject's head rises up in front of the
letters so the title sits behind her.
Directly above the title, one line of small, widely-spaced capitals in flat charcoal-black — part of
the monochrome palette, not red — centred, reading exactly three city names separated by a
centred middle dot: NEW YORK · LONDON · MILAN. Use that exact dot character between
each city, not a comma. Spell the title and all three cities correctly. No other text, numbers, or
lettering anywhere in the image.
TONAL & LAYOUT ZONES (LEAVE ROOM FOR THE OVERLAYS)
Across the very top of the frame, keep the same flat white canvas so the red title and black city
line read crisply against it. This white extends unbroken into the top-left and top-right corners,
exactly the same flat value as everywhere else — no separate patch, square, card, or panel of
any kind sits apart from it. Keep the upper-left background calm and empty, free of any pattern,
object, or texture. NOTE FOR PRODUCTION: the lower-centre of the frame is the dark navy
suit, not a light tone — any headline placed there needs to be light or white to stay legible. The
far-left and far-right thirds of the frame stay as quiet, continuous white backdrop.
MOOD
Timeless, powerful, refined, iconic, quietly self-assured — with one confident, editorial pop of
red as the signature mark, not a loud or busy colour treatment.

Final Check
The frame is a true 3:4 portrait, wider than it is tall, filled edge to edge.
The subject's face matches the uploaded reference photograph exactly.
Hairstyle matches the reference photo's actual cut/length/texture, not a generic bob.
Glasses appear only if the reference photo shows them.
The subject is centred and carried large; the face sits near the horizontal centre.
The chair and body are turned to a slight three-quarter angle (not square-on), legs crossed,
elbow on the raised knee, hand to the chin, face turned back to the lens.
The image reads as classic black-and-white photography. The only colour anywhere in the
frame is the red masthead lettering — no colour leak onto skin, hair, suit, chair, or background.
The title reads ICON as one solid, unbroken word — four letters, correctly spelled, no hyphen or
gap, clean and undistorted Didone, centred, in a rich publication red, contained fully within the
letters.
The city line reads NEW YORK · LONDON · MILAN — three cities, correctly spelled, centred
directly above the title, in charcoal-black.
The subject's head overlaps the title so it sits behind the head.
The background is a flat, seamless white backdrop with no grain or texture of its own —
corners, edges, and centre all equally bright, with no dimmer patch, greyer patch, or isolated
white square anywhere, including both top corners.
No warm or coloured tint bleeds from the red masthead letters into the white background around
them.
The suit is a rich midnight navy — not black, not grey, not white or pale — reading with strong,
clean tonal contrast against the white backdrop, no merging, no loss of separation.
The backdrop is continuous and seamless edge to edge — no join, no fold line, no patchwork of
different shades.
No text other than the title and city line. A single subject, one clear well-lit face, hands natural
and correct.
